_comment: Structural formulae. Not string-matchable as vocabulary; caught by pattern. These survive every vocabulary ban, which is why a wordlist alone does not work.

negation_correction.note: The single most reliable machine-prose tell. Sets up a strawman to knock down. 'X isn't just Y, it's Z.'

not_x_but_y.note: Bare form of the same move.

less_x_than_y.note: Comparative variant. 'Less a protocol than a promise.'

it_is_not_that.note: 'It's not that X; it's that Y.'

causal_subject_has_no.note: A causal clause makes an explicit subject possess an absence before stating the result. Report the form for rewrite; the claim may still be factually correct.

whether_or.note: False-choice scaffolding. Absorbed from slopbeth STRUCTURE_PATTERNS. Signal only: fires on genuine enumerations.

from_x_to_y_sweep.note: Fake-range gesture. 'From governance to settlement.' Absorbed from slopbeth. Signal only: fires on genuine enumerations.

rule_of_three.note: Tidy triad. One or two is prose; a habit of three is a formula. Signal only: fires on genuine enumerations.

em_dash.note: Per the author's own slopbeth rule. Use a comma, colon, semicolon, or bracket.

bold_lead_bullet.note: '**Thing**: explanation' bullet. Skill-checklist shape leaking into prose.

title_case_heading.note: Headings In Title Case Like This.

unrequested_tldr.note: Only permitted when the user asked for one.

apology_theatre.note: Absorbed from slopgent. Apology in place of a cause and a fix.

unearned_we.note: Agent adopting the user's first person plural on work the agent did not do.

cadence.note: Rhythm tells. Reported as signals, not defects: judgement required.
